parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A boat crosses a river. The boat points at right angles to the river bank and it travels at a
speed of 3.5 m / s relative to the water.
A river current acts at right angles to the direction the boat points. The river current has a
speed of 2.5 m / s.
By drawing a scale diagram or by calculation, determine the speed and direction of the boat
relative to the river bank.
speed = ______
direction relative to the river bank = ______

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Speed is a scalar quantity and velocity is a vector quantity.
State the names of one other scalar quantity and one other vector quantity.
scalar quantity ______
vector quantity ______

text: Fig. 2.1 shows a ship loaded with containers.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The containers with the greatest mass are loaded near the bottom of the ship.
State and explain the effect on the stability of the ship of loading the containers in this way.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:

energy = ______

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A wind turbine has a maximum output power of 1.8 MW. The turbine operates at maximum
power for 4.0 h.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Define the unit kW h.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the energy produced by the wind turbine operating at maximum power for
4.0 h. Give your answer in kW h.
energy = ______ kW h

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Radiation from the Sun is the main source of energy for most of our energy resources.
State two energy resources that are not due to radiation from the Sun.

text: The density of steel is 7800 kg / m and the density of water is 1000 kg / m .
Explain why the ship floats in the water.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Thermal energy is transferred through the metal pan by conduction.
State and explain the two ways that thermal energy is conducted in a metal.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
The water boils and leaves the liquid as a gas.
Explain, in terms of forces and distances between particles, why the gas occupies a
much greater volume than it does as a liquid.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: State two ways in which boiling differs from evaporation.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The water is replaced with 200 cm of milk.
The initial temperature of the milk is 20.0°C. The boiling point of milk is 95.0°C.
The milk starts to boil when 60 700 J of thermal energy has been transferred to it. The density
of milk is 1.03 g / cm .
Calculate the value of the specific heat capacity of milk. Give your answer to 3 significant
figures.
specific heat capacity = ______

compression ______
rarefaction ______

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
We can see light from the Sun but we cannot hear any sound from it.
State the reason for this.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
During a thunderstorm, an observer sees the lightning almost immediately but hears the
sound of the thunder several seconds later. The thunder and lightning are produced at the
same time.
The sound of the thunder is heard 9.0 s after the lightning is seen. The speed of sound in air
is 340 m / s.
Calculate the distance from the thunderstorm to the observer.
distance = ______

parts.text:

Calculate the charge that flows.
charge = ______

advantage ______
disadvantage ______

parts.text:

when two nuclei of deuterium combine. An isotope of helium (He) and a neutron are formed.
Use nuclide notation to write down the nuclide equation for this reaction.
